source_title: Winding Yarn (Interior of a Nantucket Kitchen)
desc_src: Set in a rustic kitchen on Nantucket Island, Massachusetts, this painting depicts a woman who winds a ball of yarn from a coil looped in the hands of a man sitting across from her at a respectable distance. At the time, winding yarn was a common symbol of courtship that carried humorous overtones of a woman ensnaring her suitor. The second woman in the composition is likely a chaperone. The suitor’s unrefined, open-legged pose, coupled with his rude action of placing his hat on the floor, adds further comic elements that contemporary audiences would have appreciated.

The Singing Ringing Tree Pick a breezy day to visit this modern sculpture to hear the haunting sounds made by the wind funnelling through the array of pipework.

Singing Ringing Tree This is one of a number of artworks being installed in Lancashire for a project entitled 'Panopticons' (historically, circular prisons!). As the name suggests the wind blowing over the open pipes can make it 'sing', although bashing it to make it for the 'ring' may well be frowned upon. In the distance on the right you can see the Coal Clough wind farm 155316
